*Generate GitHub Actions workflows that are verified, not hoped for.*

> **Say which rung you reached, and never claim more.**

## Why install this

Every other AI workflow generator emits YAML and stops. You find out whether it
works when a push fails.

forge resolves every `uses:` against the real GitHub API, validates every `with:`
key against the action's own `action.yml`, reports how many majors behind each
pin is, then runs `actionlint` and `zizmor` — and tells you exactly which of the
three rungs it reached. About one second, end to end.

**Rung 0 is the one nothing else does.** Measured against a deliberately broken
workflow, `actionlint` caught six defect classes and missed exactly two:
`actions/checkout@v99` and `actions/setup-nodejs@v4`, an action that does not
exist. Both are signature failures of model-written YAML, and no linter checks
that a ref is real. Separately, a workflow pinning `actions/checkout@v5` passed
`actionlint` *and* `zizmor` completely clean while sitting two majors behind —
staleness is invisible to both.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/forge/SKILL.md` | The ladder, the flow, and when forge fires. |
| `skills/forge/bin/forge.js` | The CLI: `detect`, `resolve`, `verify`, `header`, `check`. |
| `skills/forge/lib/` | Ref resolution, staleness, the lint runners, the masthead. |
| `skills/forge/references/anatomy.md` | The fixed shape of a generated workflow. |
| `skills/forge/references/recipes.md` | The job shapes worth starting from. |
| `skills/forge/references/security.md` | Permissions, injection, and what `zizmor` actually catches. |
| `skills/forge/skill-invariants.json` | The prose guardrails and the baseline eval declaration. |

## Quick start

```bash
forge detect --repo .                      # what this repo already tells us
forge verify .github/workflows/ci.yml      # the ladder, and the rung it reached
forge resolve actions/checkout@v5          # a ref, resolved to a pinned SHA
```

Install from the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills),
then ask for the workflow you want.

## Triggers

- "set up CI"
- "add a workflow"
- "my workflow is broken"
- "why is my action failing"
- "pin my actions"
- "audit my workflows"
- Creating, fixing, hardening or speeding up any GitHub Actions workflow — a
  release or publish job, a deploy, a matrix build, a scheduled job.

## Requirements

- Node 18+.
- [`gh`](https://cli.github.com/), authenticated. Rung 0 resolves refs through
  the GitHub API, and an unauthenticated run is rate-limited into uselessness.
- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) and
  [`zizmor`](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor) for rungs 1 and 2. A missing
  tool is reported as a rung not reached, never as a rung that passed.

## The ladder

| Rung | Checks | Catches | Tool |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | every `uses:` resolves; every `with:` key is real; how stale the pin is | hallucinated actions, dead refs, misspelled inputs, 3-majors-behind pins | `gh api` |
| 1 | syntax, expressions, contexts, shell | ~everything structural | `actionlint` |
| 2 | injection, permissions, pinning, credential persistence | the security class | `zizmor` |

## Development

```bash
cd skills/forge/skills/forge
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / forge` runs the same tests plus the house lints on every pull
request, and `smith verify --skill forge` reports which rung of the skill ladder
it has reached.
